original_question: For each integer n >= 2 and each n-tuple of real numbers theta_1, ..., theta_n, must one always have lim inf_{q -> +infty} q * ||q theta_1|| * ... * ||q theta_n|| = 0? In other words, does the multidimensional Littlewood-type statement hold for every set of n real numbers once n is at least 2?
target_in_paper: Section 1, equation (2): the unnumbered multidimensional analogue of Littlewood's conjecture for a fixed integer n > 2. ([studocu.com](https://www.studocu.com/hk/document/hong-kong-university-of-science-and-technology/general-physics-with-calculus/on-open-problems-in-diophantine-approximation-1202/146248134))
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the multiplicative lim-inf expression q·||q theta_1||·...·||q theta_n|| and the universal quantification over real n-tuples, and it asks the same basic yes/no problem discussed in the paper's multidimensional Littlewood-type extension. ([studocu.com](https://www.studocu.com/hk/document/hong-kong-university-of-science-and-technology/general-physics-with-calculus/on-open-problems-in-diophantine-approximation-1202/146248134))
missing_details: In the paper, this is posed only for a fixed integer n > 2; the case n = 2 is treated separately as the classical Littlewood conjecture in equation (1), while n = 1 is explicitly excluded. ([studocu.com](https://www.studocu.com/hk/document/hong-kong-university-of-science-and-technology/general-physics-with-calculus/on-open-problems-in-diophantine-approximation-1202/146248134))

The variable q ranges over positive integers; the lim inf is taken along q in Z_{>0} with q -> +infty. ([studocu.com](https://www.studocu.com/hk/document/hong-kong-university-of-science-and-technology/general-physics-with-calculus/on-open-problems-in-diophantine-approximation-1202/146248134))

The notation ||x|| must be defined as the distance from x to the nearest integer. ([studocu.com](https://www.studocu.com/hk/document/hong-kong-university-of-science-and-technology/general-physics-with-calculus/on-open-problems-in-diophantine-approximation-1202/146248134))

To be fully paper-faithful, the question should be stated as a standalone multidimensional analogue of Littlewood's conjecture, not as a reformulation that merges it with the n = 2 case. ([studocu.com](https://www.studocu.com/hk/document/hong-kong-university-of-science-and-technology/general-physics-with-calculus/on-open-problems-in-diophantine-approximation-1202/146248134))

The problem itself assumes no extra hypotheses such as linear independence, algebraicity, or bad approximability of theta_1, ..., theta_n; those appear only in nearby discussion and in the special-case positive result of Theorem 1. ([studocu.com](https://www.studocu.com/hk/document/hong-kong-university-of-science-and-technology/general-physics-with-calculus/on-open-problems-in-diophantine-approximation-1202/146248134))
refined_question: Fix an integer n > 2. Is it true that for every n-tuple of real numbers theta_1, ..., theta_n one has lim inf as q -> +infty, with q ranging over positive integers, of q·||q theta_1||·...·||q theta_n|| equal to 0, where ||x|| denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer? ([studocu.com](https://www.studocu.com/hk/document/hong-kong-university-of-science-and-technology/general-physics-with-calculus/on-open-problems-in-diophantine-approximation-1202/146248134))
justification: Your draft is targeting the sentence in Section 1 immediately after the classical two-variable Littlewood conjecture: the paper states that the 'similar multidimensional problem' is, for given n > 2, whether lim inf q->+infty q·||q theta_1||·...·||q theta_n|| = 0 for all real theta_1, ..., theta_n. The main mismatch is that your draft folds in n = 2, whereas the paper treats n = 2 separately as equation (1) and reserves equation (2) for n > 2. The nearby Theorem 1 then gives a special affirmative case for tuples coming from a basis of a real algebraic field of degree n + 1, confirming that equation (2) is exactly the intended open problem in this local context. ([studocu.com](https://www.studocu.com/hk/document/hong-kong-university-of-science-and-technology/general-physics-with-calculus/on-open-problems-in-diophantine-approximation-1202/146248134))
